theorem contractedSize_eq_two_iff (t : IncreasingBoundaryTriple n) (hn : 3 ≤ n) :
    t.contractedSize = 2 ↔ t.spanInterval = fullBoundaryInterval hn := by
  constructor
  · intro hs
    have hb := t.contractedSize_bounds
    have hl : t.lower.val = 0 := by omega
    have hu : t.upper.val = n - 1 := by
      have hu := t.upper.isLt
      have hlt := lt_trans t.lower_middle t.middle_upper
      change t.lower.val < t.upper.val at hlt
      unfold contractedSize erasedInteriorCount at hs
      omega
    apply BoundaryInterval.eq_of_endpoints
    · apply Fin.ext
      exact hl
    · apply Fin.ext
      exact hu
  · intro he
    have hl := congrArg (fun I : BoundaryInterval n => I.left.val) he
    have hu := congrArg (fun I : BoundaryInterval n => I.right.val) he
    change t.lower.val = 0 at hl
    change t.upper.val = n - 1 at hu
    unfold contractedSize erasedInteriorCount
    rw [hl, hu]
    omega

theorem child_product_difference (π : IntervalComposition I) (J : BoundaryInterval n)
    (X₁ X₂ : IntervalArray n R)
    (h : ∀ K, ¬ (K.left ≤ J.left ∧ J.right ≤ K.right) → X₁ K = X₂ K)
    (k : Fin π.parts) (hk : (π.part k).left ≤ J.left ∧ J.right ≤ (π.part k).right) :
    (∏ l : Fin π.parts, X₂ (π.part l)) - (∏ l : Fin π.parts, X₁ (π.part l)) =
      (X₂ (π.part k) - X₁ (π.part k)) *
        ∏ l ∈ Finset.univ.erase k, X₁ (π.part l) := by
  classical
  have hp : (∏ l ∈ Finset.univ.erase k, X₂ (π.part l)) =
      ∏ l ∈ Finset.univ.erase k, X₁ (π.part l) := by
    apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
    intro l hl
    exact (h _ (π.other_part_excludes J k hk l (Finset.mem_erase.mp hl).1)).symm
  rw [← Finset.mul_prod_erase Finset.univ (fun l => X₂ (π.part l)) (Finset.mem_univ k)]
  rw [← Finset.mul_prod_erase Finset.univ (fun l => X₁ (π.part l)) (Finset.mem_univ k)]
  rw [hp]
  ring

source_fidelity_assessments.assessment: Write x=t.lower.val and z=t.upper.val. Strict x<middle<z gives z>=x+2, so the erased count z-x-1 is positive and counts exactly the strictly interior integer positions. Since z<n, subtraction cannot remove either endpoint and n-(z-x-1)>=x+2; the count is at most n and strictly below n. This models contracting the whole critical arc to one leaf. It does not delete the endpoints or merely the named middle vertex.

Expansion fixes k<=x and sends k>x to k+(z-x-1). Fin bounds follow from k<n-(z-x-1). On each side this is strictly increasing, and across the branch its value increases as well. The consecutive contracted positions x and x+1 expand to exactly the old endpoints x and z. Its range is confined to positions <=x or >=z. The independent range/deletion consumers additionally prove that precisely the open interval (x,z) is absent, including the critical middle, and that every surviving position occurs uniquely.

The inverse is defined only for physical survivors. It fixes an old position <=x and subtracts the erased count from an old position >=z. The survivor hypothesis makes the subtraction and branch selection exact; it is not an assumed inverse equation. Both round trips follow by branch arithmetic, and the equivalence uses those actual maps. The independent consumers verify the full subtype cardinality, every survivor's unique preimage and order preservation, so an arbitrary same-cardinality equivalence would not suffice.

The first contracted position expands to old position 0. Bounds force the last contracted position into the shifted branch; m-1+(n-m)=n-1 proves the final old position. Thus both ends of the complete linear boundary word survive. These are position identities; an actual contracted geometric tuple, directed closing-edge equality and physical-root identification still need their own definitions/proofs.

If the contracted size is 2, the lower-bound inequality forces x=0 and the size formula forces z=n-1. BoundaryInterval equality is then obtained from those exact endpoints. Conversely the full-span endpoint equations give size 2. Combining size>=2 with the negation of this equivalence yields size>=3 for a proper critical span. The original hn>=3 requirement is necessary only to name the canonical full interval and loses no triple domain. The two-position full-span case is retained as a formal one-leaf word, without introducing a two-gon amplitude.

For ordered distinct child indices k<l, canonical part_order gives right(k)<=left(l). If both contained J, the endpoint inequalities would imply J.right<=J.left, contradicting the strict positive length built into BoundaryInterval. The other index order is symmetric. Thus at most one child can contain J; every different child excludes it. Shared endpoints cause no exception because containing a positive interval requires both endpoints. There is no nonunary restriction: unary compositions and a one-leaf J remain included. The independent formal-leaf consumer proves existence as well as uniqueness by half-open coverage and the integer one-leaf length.

When every child excludes J, h gives equality of each actual child coordinate and product congruence proves full-product equality. If k contains J, uniqueness supplies the premise of h for every l in univ.erase k. Therefore the complement products agree. Factoring each full product as its k factor times that complement and distributing subtraction yields exactly (X₂(k)-X₁(k)) times the old complement. No division or nonzero assumption is used, so zero coordinates are included. Independent consumers prove the equivalent new-side complement formula, annihilation by a zero unaffected factor, and specialization to the actual canonical farOnlyCoordinates under the proved off-critical locality theorem.
